background.working_life: A full-time employee of fifty, working in the construction and building trades within the manufacturing sector, with a working base at or from home rather than a distant site or plant. Typical weeks run between thirty-one and forty-eight hours, arranged around orders and drawings rather than fixed shifts. There are no supervisory or management duties, and the role sits among routine occupations, though a degree-level qualification was gained earlier. Commuting costs nothing, and the day begins where it ends.
background.home_and_household: Home is a terraced house in a suburban part of the South East, owned with a mortgage still running. Three adults share it: a married couple in an opposite-sex partnership, plus one further adult, with no dependent children, so any offspring are grown. The number of bedrooms matches what the household requires exactly, leaving no spare room and no crowding. Working from the same address means the property serves as both dwelling and workplace, requiring some care over storage, tools and quiet.
background.week_and_hobbies: Without a commute, the week has a fairly settled rhythm: an early start, a defined stretch of hours, and evenings free at home or in the surrounding streets and parks. Practical interests carry over from trade skills, with repairs, joinery and improvements around the terraced house filling weekends. Time is also given to the other adults in the household, occasional trips further into the South East, and quieter pursuits such as radio, reading, motoring or watching sport at the weekend.
